story-star-cap-0.text: Eric found a tiny red cap beneath a fern. Inside it slept a little fox named Pip. Above them, one small star blinked.

hint-a.text: Open your mouth wide. Make the short a sound in apple.

sound-b.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-b.text: Close your lips, then pop them open. Keep it short. No extra uh.

sound-c.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-c.text: Lift the back of your tongue, then release a tiny puff. No extra uh.

sound-d.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-d.text: Touch your tongue just behind your top teeth, then let it pop down. No extra uh.

sound-e.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-e.text: Open your mouth a little. Make the short e sound in egg.

sound-f.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-f.text: Rest your top teeth on your bottom lip. Blow gently. Your voice stays quiet.

sound-g.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-g.text: Use the back of your tongue for a quick voiced pop. No extra uh.

sound-h.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-h.text: Open your mouth and breathe out softly, as if warming your hands.

sound-i.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-i.text: Relax your mouth. Make the short i sound at the start of itch.

sound-j.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-j.text: Start with your tongue near the roof of your mouth, then release with your voice.

sound-k.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-k.text: Use the back of your tongue for a quick quiet pop. No extra uh.

sound-l.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-l.text: Put the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth. Let your voice hum around it.

hint-m.text: Close your lips and hum. Keep your voice going without adding uh.

sound-n.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-n.text: Put your tongue behind your top teeth and hum through your nose.

sound-o.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-o.text: Drop your jaw and open your mouth. Make the short o sound in American English.

sound-p.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-p.text: Close your lips and release a tiny quiet puff. Keep it short. No extra uh.

sound-qu.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-qu.text: Q usually travels with u. Together here they make two sounds: k, then w.

sound-r.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-r.text: Curl or bunch your tongue gently inside your mouth. Keep it away from your teeth.

sound-s.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-s.text: Keep your teeth close. Let air slide out like a soft hiss. Your voice stays quiet.

hint-t.text: Tap your tongue behind your top teeth. Make a tiny quiet pop. No extra uh.

sound-u.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-u.text: Relax your mouth. Make the short u sound at the start of up.

sound-v.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-v.text: Touch your top teeth to your bottom lip. Blow gently and turn your voice on.

sound-w.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-w.text: Round your lips, then let them relax as you turn on your voice.

sound-x.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-x.text: X at the end of box stands for two sounds: k, then s.

sound-y.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-y.text: Lift the middle of your tongue, then glide into the next sound. This is y in yes.

sound-z.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-z.text: Keep your teeth close and buzz with your voice on.

sound-sh.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-sh.text: Round your lips a little. Let air flow softly. Two letters work together for one sound.

sound-ch.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-ch.text: Start with your tongue near the roof of your mouth, then release a short quiet puff. Two letters, one sound.

sound-th.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-th.text: Place your tongue gently between your teeth and blow. This is the quiet th in thin.

sound-ck.source: eSpeak NG en-us, isolated by phoneme event

hint-ck.text: At the end of duck, c and k work together for one quick sound. No extra uh.

cue-welcome.text: Hi, Eric! Welcome to your reading quest. We will tap the sounds, slide them together, and read. You can ask for help any time.

cue-practice.text: Let’s practice reading, Eric. Start with a sound, then make a word.

cue-oral.text: A word is hiding in these sounds, Eric. Listen without looking at letters. Put the sounds together in your head, and try saying the word. Then uncover it.

cue-sounds.text: Tap a letter to hear its sound. The little speaker can tell you how to make it.

cue-blend.text: Tap each sound from left to right. Then slide underneath to blend the sounds into a word.

cue-build.text: Listen to the word. Tap the letters in order to build it. One sound goes in each box.

cue-choose.text: Listen to the word. Read each choice, then tap the matching word. You can use the little speakers for help.

cue-sentence.text: Now read a little sentence. Tap a word if you want help. Listen, then try reading it yourself.

cue-said.text: You gave it a try, Eric! I cannot hear you. Read it once more to a grown-up if you can.

cue-correct1.text: You matched the sounds, Eric. That was careful reading!

cue-correct2.text: You kept going, Eric. Your practice is helping!

cue-correct3.text: You checked the letters from left to right. Well done, Eric!

cue-supported.text: You used a hint and kept trying. That is how readers learn, Eric.

cue-retry.text: Let’s look closely, Eric. Listen to the sounds, one at a time. You can try again.

cue-buildRetry.text: Let’s change that sound. Look at the glowing box, listen again, and try a letter.

cue-done.text: You finished your little reading quest, Eric! Your effort earned a new leaf for your reading tree.

cue-storyIntro.text: Let’s listen to a story, Eric. The words will glow as I read. Tap a word to hear it again.

cue-yourTurn.text: Your turn, Eric. Try reading the big words. Tap a word or the speaker if you want help.

cue-storyDone.text: You followed a whole story, Eric! Tell a grown-up your favorite part.

cue-storyQuestion.text: Let’s think about our story. Listen to the question, then choose an answer.

cue-storyRetry.text: Let’s think about what happened. You can listen to the story again, then try another answer.

cue-home.text: Your reading garden. Choose a little quest, practice sounds, or listen to a story.

lesson-team.text: The Sound Bridge. Two letters, one sound.

question-star-cap.text: What helped the star find its way home?

option-star-cap-0.text: The map and the moon gate

story-star-cap-1.text: The star drifted down like a feather. It had forgotten the way home. Eric held out the cap, and the star landed softly inside.

story-star-cap-2.text: Pip unrolled a little map. A silver path led up the hill. Eric carried the star carefully while Pip padded beside him.

story-star-cap-3.text: At the top stood a sleepy moon gate. Eric tapped it three times. The gate opened just wide enough for one small star.

story-star-cap-4.text: The star rose through the gate and shone over the forest. One warm beam settled on the red cap. Pip gave a happy little bow.

story-star-cap-5.text: Eric put the cap beside the fern. Pip curled up inside. Every night, the little star blinked twice to say thank you.

question-moon-seed.text: What helped the magic seed grow?

story-moon-seed-0.text: In a quiet garden, Eric found a silver seed. Pip sniffed it. A gentle voice from the watering can said, This seed grows when someone is kind.

story-moon-seed-1.text: Eric made a small hole. Pip tucked the seed into the soft earth. Together they gave it water, then sat nearby to wait.

story-moon-seed-2.text: A beetle needed help crossing a puddle. Eric laid down a leaf bridge. In the garden, the silver seed gave its first tiny wiggle.

story-moon-seed-3.text: A bird had dropped a feather. Eric placed it safely beside the nest. A green shoot appeared where the seed had been.

story-moon-seed-4.text: That evening, a pale flower opened. Its petals glowed like moonlight. Eric and Pip watched in silence while the garden filled with a soft silver shine.

story-moon-seed-5.text: The watering can smiled. Small kind things help wonderful things grow, it said. Eric left a little water for the next thirsty visitor.

question-boat-wish.text: Why did the boat make room for the frog?

option-boat-wish-0.text: To help a friend get home

story-boat-wish-0.text: Eric folded a little paper boat. Pip watched from a flat stone. The boat whispered that it wished to see the other side of the pond.

story-boat-wish-1.text: Eric set the boat on the still water. A breeze filled its paper sail. Pip followed along the bank, carrying a small red flag.

story-boat-wish-2.text: The boat stopped beside a water lily. A tiny frog was looking for a ride. The boat made room, and the frog climbed carefully aboard.

story-boat-wish-3.text: Near the reeds, the breeze grew quiet. Eric gently fanned the air with a leaf. The little sail filled again, and the boat moved on.

story-boat-wish-4.text: At last, the boat reached a smooth pebble beach. The frog hopped home. The boat had crossed the pond and helped a friend along the way.

story-boat-wish-5.text: Eric carried the little boat back to its shelf. Pip curled up below it. Tomorrow, they would find another small adventure to share.
